### Problem

Security is checked only by models, after the code is written. While it codes, the autopilot reviews its own change with the model against the whole review profile, and then the paid review looks for the same holes again; what it finds costs a fix round and one more review. In the engine's runs from 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-22, fix rounds after the review took 69 of the 178 model minutes (39%), more than writing the code (57). No repository runs a deterministic check for leaked secrets, insecure code (OWASP Top 10), dependencies with known vulnerabilities or unsafe GitHub workflows, except what the `wordpress-plugin` kind already runs (Psalm taint analysis, the WordPress coding standards' security sniffs, Plugin Check) and an opt-in CodeQL in three public plugins. The `ai-agent-plugin` kind, the engine and the repositories with no kind run none.

### Scope

- One security gate for every repository, whatever its kind: leaked secrets (gitleaks), insecure code with the OWASP Top 10 and language rules (Semgrep), dependencies with known vulnerabilities (osv-scanner) and GitHub workflows (zizmor). Each tool pinned to a version, its rules and severities as data, never hard-wired to one kind; a kind's own checks stay as they are.
- It runs in three places with the same command: inside `make pre-pr` (so the autopilot and anyone who codes runs it and fixes what it finds before the pull request), as a required check of the pull request (people and forks too, with no secrets), and its result in the review's brief, where the review is told those classes are already checked and spends its attention on the logic.
- Brakes, each one a criterion: it reads only what the change adds or modifies, and a finding in code the change did not touch never fails it; its report to the agent is cut to 30 findings or 8 KB; the autopilot gets at most 2 attempts at the same finding, then writes a suppression with its reason (the kind's suppressions file) or stops with `finish stop`; and one organisation setting, `security-gate: off | report | block`, starts at `report` (it shows, it never fails) and moves to `block` by a person's change to the policy.
- Docs (docs/testing-and-quality.md, docs/workflows.md, kinds/README.md, the packs, CONTRIBUTING.md) and tests in step.

### Out of scope

- Moving the setting to `block`: a later change, after a week of `report`.
- The kind's own checks (Psalm, PHPCS, Plugin Check, CodeQL).
- The documentation check and the impact map (separate issues).

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given a change that adds a secret, an OWASP Top 10 pattern of high severity, a dependency with a known critical or high vulnerability, or an unsafe workflow (an untrusted value inside `run:`), when `make pre-pr` runs in a repository of any kind or of no kind, then the gate names each finding with its file, line, rule and fix.
- C2: Given a finding in a line the change did not add or modify, when the gate runs, then it is listed as pre-existing and never fails the gate.
- C3: Given `security-gate: report`, when the gate finds something, then `make pre-pr` and the pull request's check pass with the findings in their output; given `block`, then both fail on a high or critical one; given `off`, then the gate does not run.
- C4: Given the autopilot meets the same finding after 2 attempts, when it runs again, then it writes a suppression with its reason or runs `finish stop`, and never a third attempt.
- C5: Given more than 30 findings, when the agent reads the report, then it gets the 30 most severe and the count of the rest, within 8 KB.
- C6: Given a pull request, when the review builds its brief, then the brief carries the gate's result and the review's prompt says which classes the gate already checks.
- C7: Given a fork's pull request, when the gate runs, then it runs with no secrets and no write token.

### Criticality

Critical
